record.context_brief: Core partitions with parts divisible by ℓ
record.original_question: For positive integers s and ℓ, is the number of (s, s+1)-core partitions whose parts are all multiples of ℓ equal to the closed form stated in Conjecture 11.7, which specializes to the Catalan number when ℓ = 1?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 11.7. The number of (s, s+1)-core partitions λ with parts that are multiples of ℓ equals ... In particular, if ℓ = 1 then this count is the Catalan number C_s.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let s and ℓ be positive integers. A partition λ = (λ_1 ≥ λ_2 ≥ … ≥ λ_k > 0) is called a t-core if none of the hook lengths of its Young diagram is divisible by t. A partition is an (s, s+1)-core if it is simultaneously an s-core and an (s+1)-core.

Write s = kℓ + r with 0 ≤ r < ℓ. Define the Raney numbers
   R_{p,q}(n) = (q / (np + q)) · C(np + q, n).

Prove or disprove the following statement: the number of (s, s+1)-core partitions all of whose parts are multiples of ℓ equals
   R_{ℓ+1, ℓ-r}(k+1) · (something explicit in s, ℓ),
or more precisely, equals the closed-form expression that specializes, when ℓ = 1, to the Catalan number C_s = (1/(s+1)) C(2s, s).

Equivalently: determine and prove the closed form, conjectured to be expressible via Raney numbers, for the cardinality of the set of (s, s+1)-core partitions whose parts all lie in ℓℤ_{>0}, and verify that it reduces to C_s when ℓ = 1.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture was confirmed: a 2015 preprint by Du, Huang and Yan ("The Raney Numbers and (s,s+1)-Core Partitions", arXiv:1512.08080) proves Amdeberhan's conjecture, showing that the number of (s,s+1)-core partitions with parts that are multiples of ℓ is given by Raney numbers, recovering the Catalan number when ℓ = 1.

status_evidence.title: The Raney Numbers and (s,s+1)-Core Partitions
status_evidence.snippet: We confirm a conjecture posed by Amdeberhan concerning the enumeration of (s,s+1)-core partitions λ with parts that are multiples of p.
status_evidence.claim: Amdeberhan's conjecture on (s,s+1)-cores with parts divisible by ℓ has been proven, with the count given by Raney numbers.

status_evidence.title: On the Enumeration of (s, s+1, s+2)-Core Partitions
status_evidence.snippet: Related results on simultaneous core partitions and Catalan/Raney enumerations.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms the area is well-developed with the (s,s+1)-core/Catalan link established.
